title: The Windows of Heaven
old_p1: The Lord asked His people to pay tithing. Tithing means giving back one part out of every ten to the Lord.
In Malachi’s day, people grew their food. They brought one part to the storehouse. A storehouse was a room for keeping food at the Lord’s house.
The Lord said, “Prove me.” That means, “Try it, and see what I will do.”
old_p2: He promised to “open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing.” Malachi’s land was dry, so rain from the sky was a big blessing. The Lord pours down blessings like rain.
Children can pay tithing too, one coin out of every ten. Tonight, count three blessings on your fingers before you sleep.
p1: In Malachi’s day, people grew their own food. The Lord asked them to pay tithing: one part of every ten, given back.
They brought it to the storehouse, a room for food at the Lord’s house. But many people had stopped bringing it.
So the Lord said, “Prove me.” He meant, “Try it, and see what I will do.”
p2: He promised to open “the windows of heaven” and “pour you out a blessing.” Rain falls from the sky and makes food grow. The Lord would pour down blessings like rain, more than they had room for.
Children can pay tithing too, one coin out of every ten. Tonight, count three blessings on your fingers and say thank you.
